title: Principal Koszul strict replacements of completed quotient towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ use the small pro-etale site, the completed ring sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$, the constant quotient sheaves $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$ and the unbounded derived category $D(R_W)$ of sheaves of $R_W$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All quotient modules are restricted to $R_W$ along the specified limit projections. Let $W$ be any scheme and let $P$ be a K-flat complex of $R_W$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Set $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, with transitions $(t,1)$ and degree-zero quotient augmentations $\epsilon_n:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$. Tensor complexes are direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then $(A,(t))$ satisfies all the hypotheses of the adic datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is Noetherian, $A/(t)$ is additive torsion, and every $A/t^n$ is finite and perfect, with the two-term free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$. On $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the sequence $0\to R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W\to S_{W,n}\to0$ is exact through the specified projection. The maps $a_{P,n}=1_P\otimes\epsilon_n$ form a strict tower morphism
$$a_P:(P\otimes_{R_W}Q_{W,n})_{n\geq1}\longrightarrow(P\otimes_{R_W}S_{W,n})_{n\geq1}.$$
Each $a_{P,n}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every $P\otimes Q_{W,n}$ is K-flat with flat terms, and $a_P$ is an objectwise K-flat replacement of the strict reduction tower of the image of $P$ in $D(R_W)$. These assertions and the augmentations are natural for chain maps between flat-term K-flat complexes. The tower transitions on the source are $1_P\otimes(t,1)$, and those on the target are the actual quotient maps.

proof.text: The coefficient DVR theorem gives that A is a principal ideal domain and its chosen uniformizer t is nonzero. Thus A is Noetherian. The finite coefficient quotient theorem gives finiteness of A/(t)^(n+1). In particular every element of the additive group of A/(t) has finite order, so that quotient is additive torsion.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; the extending absolute value and finite quotients are supplied by the cited coefficient nodes.

proof.text: Multiplication by t^(n+1) is injective because A is a domain and t is nonzero. The kernel of the quotient map is the principal ideal generated by t^(n+1), and the quotient map is surjective. Reuse the existing standard-quotients-perfect theorem: its explicit bounded complex has finite free terms and its augmentation becomes an isomorphism in the derived category. Transport its quasi-isomorphism through the standard localization to obtain the perfectness field of the adic datum, with ideal exactly (t).

For every site object U, the projection kills the indicated power of the constant uniformizer by the limit-cone equation and the constant quotient formula. Uniformizer regularity makes multiplication injective on completed sections; projection divisibility says every section in the kernel is such a multiple. The constant quotient map is sectionwise surjective (it is a constant-sheaf image of a surjection of sets), and it factors through the completion projection. Therefore the sequence is sectionwise short exact as additive sheaves. Exactness of presheaves follows by evaluation and homology; faithful exact forgetful functors reflect short exactness first to additive sheaves and then to module sheaves. Its cokernel universal property identifies the specified cokernel.desc comparison with the unique cokernel isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 093J, lemma-constant-exact, and 093M, lemma-completion-flat, applied at every ideal power.

proof.text: The only nonzero cohomology of $Q_{W,n}$ can be in degrees $-1,0$. Step 3 makes the former zero and identifies the latter with $S_{W,n}$ by the degree-zero projection. Hence the specified augmentation $\epsilon_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Both nonzero terms of $Q_{W,n}$ are flat: tensoring with the unit module $R_W$ is naturally the identity, hence exact; zero terms are flat as well. The bounded-above flat-complex theorem now makes $Q_{W,n}$ K-flat. This uses a theorem for ringed sites, with no assumption that the site has enough points.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; cohomology and augmentation computed from step 3.

proof.text: The principal Koszul tower definition applies to $\mathcal O=R_W$. Its cokernel $B_n$ is identified with $S_{W,n}$ by step 3. The map $Q_{W,n+1}\to Q_{W,n}$ is a chain map because $t^n t=t^{n+1}$. Its augmentation square commutes: in degree zero the two maps are $\pi_n=q_{n+1,n}\pi_{n+1}$, the defining limit equation, and in degree $-1$ both augmentations are zero. More generally the composite from level $b$ to $a$ has components $(t^{b-a},1)$, and quotient transitions compose as actual quotient maps. Tensoring these equalities with $P$ gives the strict tower morphism $a_P$, with exactly the source and target transitions in the statement. These are equalities of chain maps before localization.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, principal tower; explicit augmentation and transition calculation.

proof.text: Apply K-flat tensor invariance to the quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon_n$ and the given K-flat complex $P$. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon_n\otimes1_P:Q_{W,n}\otimes P\to S_{W,n}[0]\otimes P$. To use the order in the statement, conjugate by the signed interchange $p\otimes q\mapsto(-1)^{ij}q\otimes p$ for degrees $i,j$. Its inverse has the same sign. In the differential formula, the $d_P$ contributions have sign $(-1)^{(i+1)j}$ on either side, and the $d_Q$ contributions have sign $(-1)^{ij}$ on either side, so this is a chain isomorphism. It is natural for degree-zero chain maps, so the conjugate is exactly $1_P\otimes\epsilon_n=a_{P,n}$. Thus each level of the strict tower map is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; signed interchange checked with the total differential.

proof.text: Use the total-tensor model module's proved totalFlat helper for termwise flatness. For K-flatness, let H be an acyclic complex. The K-flatness of P makes H tensor P acyclic, and the K-flatness of Q makes (H tensor P) tensor Q acyclic. The existing total-tensor associator identifies this with H tensor (P tensor Q). Thus P tensor Q is K-flat without a boundedness assumption on P. A generic private helper carries out this argument and the signed-braiding argument of step 6 before specializing to the completed ring, preventing its inverse-limit definition from being unfolded repeatedly.

source.place: Tag 07A2, lemma-tensor-product-K-flat; flat tensor terms from sites-modules.tex Tag 0G6Q, lemma-tensor-flats.

proof.text: The target tower is, by definition, total tensor P with the actual restricted finite coefficient sheaves, using the actual quotient transitions. Step 5 gives the strict map, step 6 gives the component quasi-isomorphisms, and step 7 gives flat-term K-flat sources. Naturality for every chain map f:P to P' is the naturality identity of the two-variable total tensor functor, evaluated at the augmentation. This is equality before localization, hence gives naturality for the stated K-flat representatives. As noted in the stage-2 review, bridges from this actual quotient tower to other presentations of adic reduction towers belong to its citers; the declarations here do not change their coefficient conventions.
